title: Provenance: Know Where the Thing Lives

intelligence.essence: Every claim about a thing depends on knowing where the thing authoritatively lives — and this block caught each way that knowledge fails: a document "lost" that was sitting unmerged on a recovery branch (SN-0499), a live page whose source exists in no repo (SN-0501), a ratified contract that lived only on an unmerged branch while memory placed it on main (SN-0451), a number naming two different notes (SN-0545), a ledger claiming a migration the unreachable database alone could settle (SN-0445). The discipline: read the canonical store before classifying (SN-0411), re-anchor every cited artifact on the live tip, and treat the registry as the identity authority — resolving collisions by renumbering, never deletion, never a second entry (SN-0545).
intelligence.human_view: Before you can fix, verify, or even argue about anything, you have to know where it lives and which copy is the real one. This block is a catalog of what happens when that knowledge is assumed instead of proven: audits run against contracts that weren't on main, losses mourned over documents sitting in a branch, fixes prepared for pages nobody could source, a database whose truth nobody on the team could reach. The discipline that emerges — anchor on the live tip, read the canonical store, let the registry name things, and say UNKNOWN when the truth is out of reach — is the quiet foundation under every louder virtue in this corpus.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine a big library. A book can be "missing" three different ways: it's on a cart waiting to be shelved (not lost!), it's in a different building entirely (you have the wrong address), or two books got the same number sticker (now nobody knows which is which). And some rooms only the librarian may enter — if you can't go in, the honest answer is "I don't know," never a guess. These notes teach you to check the cart, check the address, trust the master list for names, and never pretend you saw inside the locked room.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, it's the household wisdom of the master ledger and the deed box: the copy in the drawer is a claim; the original in the vault is the truth. When they disagree, you go to the vault — or you say plainly that you cannot, and ask the one person who can. You never rewrite another person's ledger to match your guess, and you never throw away a document just because its number duplicates another's — you give it its own number and keep the story straight.
intelligence.ai_view: On any provenance question: read the canonical store before classifying (SN-0411); expect the tripwire to bind every commit equally and repair orphans without canonizing them (SN-0432); re-anchor cited artifacts on the live tip (SN-0451); mark unreachable truth UNKNOWN and route it to the director's query (SN-0445); diff future security scans against the recorded baseline before claiming improvement (SN-0455); keep continuity on the one canonical surface and name exclusions explicitly (SN-0476); run the removal-commit → branch-enumeration → blob-verify order before declaring anything lost (SN-0499); stop and ship the gating question when the source is unverified (SN-0501); resolve number collisions by owner renumbering under the registry's authority (SN-0545); and carry operative declarations with their quoted basis and their challenges intact (SN-0433).
intelligence.what_it_means: Ten notes define the corpus's geography: where truth lives (the canonical store, the live tip, the registry, the production database), how each location is reached (re-anchoring, full-row reads, the director's query), and what honesty requires when a location is unreachable or disputed (UNKNOWN, a held decision, a preserved tension). A cold reader holding only this essence can locate — or honestly fail to locate — anything the system claims to know.
whats_inside: A replay conflict is classified against the canonical store's actual contents, never from the error alone (SN-0411).
Direct-to-main content creates registry orphans regardless of who committed it; repairs are bookkeeping-exact and never canonize the anomaly (SN-0432).
Cited artifacts are re-anchored on the live tip before use — memory's path claims are leads, not evidence (SN-0451).
Unobservable truth stays UNKNOWN and routes through the director's query; ledger claims never self-promote (SN-0445).
Baselines are recorded before remediation is debated, and remediation crosses the human gate (SN-0455).
One canonical continuity surface; parallel memory systems are excluded by name (SN-0476).
Dead-on-main ≠ lost: enumerate recovery branches and verify blobs before declaring loss; restoration is a merge decision (SN-0499).
Unverified source of truth → ship the investigation and the gating question, never the fix (SN-0501).
The registry is the identity authority: collisions resolve by owner renumbering — never deletion, never a second entry (SN-0545).
Operative declarations carry their authority basis on their face, and challenges to that basis are preserved in the record (SN-0433).
